subject: Performance demo & interop stress plan
messages:
From: Evan Murray <evan.murray@acmedata.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Performance demo & interop stress plan

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the quick intro call earlier. Acme would like to schedule the architecture/deep-dive + hands-on stress run you mentioned. High level asks:
- We want a 60–90 minute session that includes 30–45 minutes of architecture walkthrough and 30–45 minutes of a controlled load test (focused on token throughput and P95 latency under sustained load).
- Target throughput: sustained ~200k tokens/minute for 10 minutes with 2x short bursts (1–2 min) up to ~400k tokens/minute.
- Latency target for our user path: p95 for first-token <= 120ms, end-to-end 99th percentile <= 800ms (we understand burst behavior may vary).
- We'll run two prompt sets: conversational queries (avg 60 tokens) and long-context summarization (avg 400 tokens). Attached is our prompt set/sample payloads.

Can you propose 2–3 windows next week (Dec 14–18) and confirm any infra requirements or service accounts you need? Also confirm whether this will be Hosted API or Dedicated nodes so we can align networking and firewall rules.

Attaching: acme-prompt-sets.csv

Appreciate it — Evan
Evan Murray
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Data Inc
--
acme-data.com
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Evan Murray <evan.murray@acmedata.com>

Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 12:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance demo & interop stress plan

Hi Evan — thanks, this is very helpful. We can run the session and meet the shape of load you describe; a few quick clarifying Qs before we lock a slot: 
- Which model family would you like us to use for the test (open model reference or a Redwood-curated variant)? If you don't have a preference we'll default to rwd-13b-q8 (balanced cost/latency) and have a 70%/30% breakdown of conversational vs long-context traffic.
- Are the payloads authenticated through your proxy (we'll need IP allowlist) or should we use our hosted endpoints?
- Do you want token accounting and cost estimates during the run? We can emit token breakdown and per-route cost in the Console during/after the test.

Proposed slots (Pacific time):
- Tue Dec 15: 09:30–11:00 PT
- Wed Dec 16: 13:00–14:30 PT
- Thu Dec 17: 11:00–12:30 PT

I'll pencil in Tue 09:30 PT unless you prefer a different slot. Internal plan: Karthik will own test plan and ramp profile; Marcus will validate Dedicated pool capacity + NVLink reservation; Neha will run pre-smoke and rollback runbook. Attaching our draft loadtest plan for visibility.

Attachments: redwood-loadtest-plan-v2.pdf

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 13:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance demo & interop stress plan (internal)

Agree with the plan — a couple of notes:
- For sustained 200k tpm with those prompt mixes, recommend target batch size 64 with dynamic batching enabled; we'll tune kernel selection to prioritize first-token latency.
- Suggest we prep a canary workload (10% of overall) that mirrors the long-context prompts to validate KV cache performance prior to the main run.
- If Acme prefers hosted endpoints, we should still reserve a Dedicated pool to avoid noisy-neighbor effects for the demo; Marcus, can you confirm if a 4-GPU NVLink slice is available Tue morning?

—Karthik

Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance demo & interop stress plan

Evan — confirmed for Tue Dec 15, 09:30–11:00 PT. Thanks for the prompt sets. Below is the consolidated plan and acceptance criteria; please reply to confirm and we'll send a calendar invite with the hookup details.

Plan summary:
- 09:30–09:45: Architecture + routing + instrumentation overview (Karthik)
- 09:45–10:00: Pre-smoke (Neha) — run a canary 10% traffic profile to validate KV caching and auth flows
- 10:00–10:40: Stepped load run — ramp to sustained 200k tokens/min for 10 minutes, with two planned 90s bursts to ~400k tokens/min
- 10:40–10:55: Cooldown + quick readout + token accounting export (Stephanie)
- 10:55–11:00: Rollback/fallback discussion (Marcus)

Infra and access notes:
- We'll allocate a 4xA100 NVLink Dedicated slice in us-west-2 for Tue 09:00–12:00 PT. Please provide a list of Acme public egress IP ranges or confirm a short VPN tunnel by EOD Mon so our infra team can allowlist.
- Default model: rwd-13b-q8; fallback: rwd-6b-int8 if memory pressure observed.
- We'll enable token-level tracing and emit a Console report after the run; include cost estimate in the artifact.

Acceptance criteria (pass/fail):
- Sustained 10-minute average >= 180k tokens/min (allowing 10% margin).
- Burst peaks reach >= 380k tokens/min during planned burst windows.
- First-token p95 <= 150ms during steady state; if p95 > 150ms we will mark as regression and halt run.

Attachments included in the invite: redwood-loadtest-plan-v2.pdf, acme-prompt-sets.csv, env-smoke-checklist.txt

Network / hook up: we will send a calendar invite with a temporary signed URL for the test endpoint and a short-runbook. If you prefer we can also run via your proxy; we'll need service account details.

Please confirm slot + IPs and whether you want us to share a short post-run readout doc (we recommend it).

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
